records.source: Καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι ποταμὸν ὕδατος ζωῆς λαμπρὸν ὡς κρύσταλλον, ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πλατείας αὐτῆς· καὶ τοῦ ποταμοῦ ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ξύλον ζωῆς ποιοῦν καρποὺς δώδεκα, κατὰ μῆνα ἕκαστον ἀποδιδοῦν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὰ φύλλα τοῦ ξύλου εἰς θεραπείαν τῶν ἐθνῶν.
records.gloss: And he showed me a river of water of life bright as crystal, coming out out of the throne of the God and of the Lamb. \v 2 In middle of the street of it and of the river on this side and on that side a tree of life producing fruits twelve, according to month each yielding the fruit of it, and the leaves of the tree for healing of the nations.
pieces: He showed me a river of the water of life, shining like crystal, which flows out from the throne of God and of the Lamb
through the middle of the city's street. On both banks of the river is the tree of life, which bears fruit twelve times, giving its fruit month by month, and its leaves bring healing to the nations.

L.1: And he showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing out of the throne of God and of the Lamb,
L.2: in the middle of its street; and on this side and on that side of the river, a tree of life producing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit each month, and the leaves of the tree [are] for the healing of the nations.

R.1: Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life. It was as clear as crystal. It flowed from the throne of God and of the Lamb
R.2: down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river was the tree of life. It grows a new crop of fruit every month, twelve times a year. Its leaves are used to heal the nations.

decisions.choice: the river and the trees: Ezekiel 47 and the garden of Eden
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw a river flowing from the temple, with trees on both banks that bear fresh fruit every month and whose leaves are for healing (Ezekiel 47:1-12). A river watered the garden of Eden, where the tree of life grew (Genesis 2:9-10). What was lost in Eden is given back (2:7; 22:14). The river flows from the throne of God and the Lamb, one throne.

decisions.choice: "in the middle of its street": with the river or with the tree
alternatives: the tree stands in the middle of the street, and on either side of the river
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between the description of the river and that of the tree, and can go with either: the river flows down the middle of the street, or the tree stands in the middle of the street and on both banks. The record follows the SBLGNT punctuation, which allows both.

decisions.choice: a tree of life on both sides: the tree, or trees of that kind
decisions.reason: ξύλον is singular, but it stands on both sides of the river. It may be used as a collective, trees of life, as in Ezekiel 47:12.

decisions.choice: leaves for the healing of the nations
decisions.reason: The nations who once followed the beast (13:7; 18:3) receive healing. The text does not say more about how.

records.heading: The river of the water of life

records.source: καὶ πᾶν κατάθεμα οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι.
records.gloss: And every accursed thing not will be any longer.
pieces: Nothing accursed will be found there any longer.

L.3: And there will no longer be any accursed thing.

R.3: Nothing there will be under God's curse anymore.

decisions.reason: After the first disobedience the ground was cursed (Genesis 3:17). Zechariah 14:11 promises that there will never again be a curse on Jerusalem. κατάθεμα means a thing devoted to destruction or under a curse.

records.source: καὶ ὁ θρόνος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου ἐν αὐτῇ ἔσται, καὶ οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ λατρεύσουσιν αὐτῷ, καὶ ὄψονται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And the throne of the God and of the Lamb in it will be, and the slaves of him will serve him, \v 4 and they will see the face of him, and the name of him on the foreheads of them.
pieces: God's throne, and the Lamb's, will stand in the city, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants will offer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} worship;
they will look upon {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will be written on their foreheads.

L.3: And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves will serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.4: and they will see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name [will be] on their foreheads.

R.3: The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city. God's servants will worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.4: They will see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will be written on their foreheads.

decisions.choice: one throne, and "his" slaves: God and the Lamb as one
decisions.reason: The throne belongs to God and the Lamb, and then the text says "his slaves will serve him", in the singular. As in 11:15, God and the Lamb are spoken of as one.

No one could see God's face and live (Exodus 33:20), yet the psalmist longed to see it (Psalm 17:15). Jesus promised that the pure in heart will see God (Matthew 5:8; compare 1 John 3:2). Now they will.
λατρεύσουσιν is the service of worship (7:15).
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: καὶ νὺξ οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι, καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν χρείαν φωτὸς λύχνου καὶ φῶς ἡλίου, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεὸς φωτίσει ἐπ’ αὐτούς, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
records.gloss: And night not will be any longer, and not they have need of light of lamp and light of sun, because Lord the God will shine upon them, and they will reign into the ages of the ages.
pieces: Night will be no more, and they will need neither the light of a lamp nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God will be their light; and they will reign forever and ever.

L.5: And there will be no more night, and they have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for [the] Lord God will shine on them, and they will reign for the ages of the ages.

R.5: There will never be night again. They will not need light from a lamp or from the sun, because the Lord God will shine on them. They will rule as kings forever and ever.

decisions.choice: God their light, and their reign forever
decisions.reason: See 21:23 and Isaiah 60:19. The priestly blessing asked that the LORD make his face shine on his people (Numbers 6:25). Daniel saw the saints receive the kingdom forever (Daniel 7:18, 27).

records.source: Καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί, καὶ ὁ κύριος, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν προφητῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει·
records.gloss: And he said to me: These the words faithful and true, and the Lord the God of the spirits of the prophets sent the angel of him to show to the slaves of him what things it is necessary to happen in quickness.
pieces: He said to me, "These words can be trusted, and they are true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the things that must happen soon.

L.6: And he said to me, "These words [are] faithful and true, and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the things that must take place soon.

R.6: The angel said to me, "These words are true, and you can trust them. The Lord God gives the prophets their messages. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants what must happen soon.

decisions.choice: the God of the spirits of the prophets
alternatives: the God of the Spirit who speaks through the prophets
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means the God who inspires the prophets' own spirits and gives them their message (compare 1 Corinthians 14:32; 2 Peter 1:21).

decisions.choice: the book ends as it began
decisions.reason: The words repeat 1:1: God sent his angel to show his slaves what must soon take place. The angel's words run on into 22:7, where Christ himself speaks.
Readable explains the phrase (m1).
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.heading: I am coming soon

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ· μακάριος ὁ τηρῶν τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου.
records.gloss: And behold I am coming quickly. Blessed the [one] keeping the words of the prophecy of the scroll this.
pieces: Look, I am coming soon! How blessed is the one who holds on to the words of the prophecy in this scroll!"

L.7: And look, I am coming soon. Blessed [is] the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this scroll."

R.7: Listen! I am coming soon. God blesses the person who obeys the words of the prophecy in this scroll."

decisions.choice: Christ's own words within the angel's message
decisions.reason: "I am coming soon" are Christ's words (22:12, 20). As the prophets moved from "thus says the LORD" to God's own "I", the angel's message turns to the voice of the one who sent him.
This is the sixth of the book's seven blessings, echoing the first (1:3).
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.
As in 1:3.

records.source: Κἀγὼ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων ταῦτα.
records.gloss: And I John the [one] hearing and seeing these things.
pieces: It was I, John, who heard and saw all this.

L.8: And I, John, [am] the one who hears and sees these things.

R.8: I, John, am the one who heard and saw all these things.

decisions.reason: John names himself, as at the beginning (1:1, 4, 9). He stands behind the book as a witness to what he heard and saw.

records.source: καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσα καὶ ἔβλεψα, ἔπεσα προσκυνῆσαι ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα.
records.gloss: And when I heard and saw, I fell to worship before the feet of the angel the showing me these things.
pieces: Having heard and seen them, I threw myself down to worship at the feet of the angel who was showing them to me.

L.8: And when I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things.

R.8: When I heard and saw them, I bowed down at the feet of the angel who had shown them to me. I was going to worship him.

decisions.reason: As in 19:10, John falls down to worship the angel and is stopped.

records.source: καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον.
records.gloss: And he says to me: See not; fellow slave of you I am and of the brothers of you the prophets and of those keeping the words of the scroll this; the God worship.
pieces: "No!" he told me. "I am God's servant, as you are, and as your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} the prophets are, and all who keep the words of this scroll. Worship God!"

L.9: And he says to me, "See [that you do] not! I am a fellow slave of yours and of your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} the prophets and of those who keep the words of this scroll. Worship God."

R.9: But he said to me, "Do not do that! I am a servant of God, just like you and the other prophets, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and everyone who obeys the words of this scroll. Worship God!"

decisions.reason: See the note on 19:10. The angel is a fellow slave with John, the prophets and all who keep the book's words.
The prophets include women (Acts 21:9).
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.

decisions.choice: God's servant (B); a servant of God (R)
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "fellow slave".

records.source: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, ὁ καιρὸς γὰρ ἐγγύς ἐστιν.
records.gloss: And he says to me: Not seal the words of the prophecy of the scroll this; the time for near is.
pieces: He also told me, "Keep the words of the prophecy in this scroll unsealed, for the time is close.

L.10: And he says to me, "Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this scroll, for the time is near.

R.10: Then he said to me, "Do not keep secret the words of the prophecy in this scroll. The time is near when these things will happen.

decisions.choice: do not seal: the opposite of Daniel
decisions.reason: Daniel was told to seal up his vision because it was for a distant time (Daniel 8:26; 12:4, 9). John's prophecy is to stay open, because the time is near (1:3). Compare 10:4, where the seven thunders were sealed.
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.

records.source: ὁ ἀδικῶν ἀδικησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ῥυπαρευθήτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ δίκαιος δικαιοσύνην ποιησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἁγιασθήτω ἔτι.
records.gloss: The [one] doing wrong let him do wrong still, and the filthy let him be filthy still, and the righteous righteousness let him do still, and the holy let him be holy still.
pieces: Whoever does wrong, let {{gender:them|him}} keep on doing wrong; whoever is filthy, let {{gender:them|him}} keep on being filthy; whoever is righteous, let {{gender:them|him}} keep on doing righteousness; whoever is holy, let {{gender:them|him}} keep on being holy."

L.11: Let the one who does wrong do wrong still, and let the filthy one be filthy still, and let the righteous one do righteousness still, and let the holy one be holy still."

R.11: Let those who do wrong keep doing wrong. Let those who are filthy keep on being filthy. Let those who do right keep living in righteousness. Let those who are holy keep on being holy."

decisions.reason: "Many shall purify themselves ... but the wicked shall act wickedly" (Daniel 12:10). With the time near, people show what they are. The words are a warning, not a wish that anyone stay in sin; the book's call to repent remains (22:17).
Righteousness is a key term, kept at every level.

records.source: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ, καὶ ὁ μισθός μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ, ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ ὡς τὸ ἔργον ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Behold I am coming quickly, and the reward of me with me, to give to each as the work is of him.
pieces: "Look, I come soon, and I bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} reward with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to pay back each person for what {{gender:they have|he has}} done.

L.12: "Look, I am coming soon, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} reward [is] with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to repay each one as {{gender:their|his}} work is.

R.12: "Listen! I am coming soon. I will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rewards with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will give each person what they deserve for what they have done.

decisions.choice: his reward with him: Isaiah 40 and 62
decisions.reason: "Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might ... his reward is with him" (Isaiah 40:10; 62:11). Christ comes with the reward God was to bring, and he gives to each according to their deeds (Psalm 62:13; Romans 2:6). His words run to the end of 22:16.
Christ is speaking of himself.

records.source: ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: I the Alpha and the O, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
pieces: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

L.13: I [am] the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

R.13: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end of all things.

decisions.reason: "The Alpha and the Omega" and "the beginning and the end" are God's titles (1:8; 21:6), and "the first and the last" is God's name in Isaiah 44:6 and Christ's in 1:17. Here Christ claims all three.

records.source: Μακάριοι οἱ πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν, ἵνα ἔσται ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς καὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν εἰσέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν πόλιν.
records.gloss: Blessed those washing the robes of them, so that will be the authority of them to the tree of the life and by the gates they may enter into the city.
pieces: How blessed are those who wash their robes! The tree of life will be theirs by right, and through the gates they will enter the city.

L.14: Blessed [are] those who wash their robes, so that they will have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.

R.14: God blesses the people who wash their robes clean. They will have the right to eat from the tree of life, and they will go through the gates into the city.

decisions.choice: the seventh blessing: those who wash their robes
decisions.reason: This is the last of the book's seven blessings. Washing robes recalls those who washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (7:14). The tree of life, lost in Eden, is open to them (2:7; 22:2).

The SBLGNT reads "those who wash their robes". Many later manuscripts read "those who do his commandments"; in Greek the two phrases look alike. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
As in 1:3.

records.source: ἔξω οἱ κύνες καὶ οἱ φάρμακοι καὶ οἱ πόρνοι καὶ οἱ φονεῖς καὶ οἱ εἰδωλολάτραι καὶ πᾶς φιλῶν καὶ ποιῶν ψεῦδος.
records.gloss: Outside the dogs and the sorcerers and the sexually immoral and the murderers and the idolaters and everyone loving and doing falsehood.
pieces: Left outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and all who love a lie and live it.

L.15: Outside [are] the dogs and the sorcerers and the sexually immoral and the murderers and the idolaters and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.

R.15: Outside the city are people who are like wild dogs. Outside are those who use magic, who commit sexual sins, who murder, who worship idols, and everyone who loves to lie and tells lies.

decisions.choice: dogs: those who are unclean and shameless
decisions.reason: In the Bible "dogs" was a word of contempt for the impure and shameless (Deuteronomy 23:18; Matthew 7:6; Philippians 3:2). It is a picture of people, not animals.
The list echoes 21:8 and 21:27: those who refuse God's ways remain outside. The gates are open (21:25), and the invitation of 22:17 still stands.

decisions.choice: people who are like wild dogs (R)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the word describes people (m1).

records.source: Ἐγὼ Ἰησοῦς ἔπεμψα τὸν ἄγγελόν μου μαρτυρῆσαι ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.
records.gloss: I Jesus sent the angel of me to testify to you these things for the churches.
pieces: I, Jesus, sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel to bear witness to you of these things for the churches.

L.16: I, Jesus, sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel to testify to you these things for the churches.

R.16: I, Jesus, have sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel to tell you these things for the churches.

decisions.reason: "You" is plural: the message is for the hearers in the churches. ἐπὶ with "the churches" may mean "for", "about" or "in" the churches; the book is addressed to them (1:4, 11).
Jesus speaks of himself.

records.source: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ῥίζα καὶ τὸ γένος Δαυίδ, ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρός, ὁ πρωϊνός.
records.gloss: I am the root and the offspring of David, the star the bright the morning.
pieces: I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright morning star."

L.16: I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright morning star."

R.16: I come from David's family, and I am also the one David's family came from. I am the bright morning star."

decisions.choice: the Root and the Offspring of David
decisions.reason: See 5:5 and Isaiah 11:1, 10. Jesus is both David's descendant and the source from which David's line came.
See 2:28. "A star shall come out of Jacob" (Numbers 24:17). The morning star announces the dawn: Christ brings the day that has no night (22:5).
Titles of the Messiah are capitalized, as in 5:5.

records.source: καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ νύμφη λέγουσιν· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ ἀκούων εἰπάτω· Ἔρχου· καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω, ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν.
records.gloss: And the Spirit and the bride say: Come. And the [one] hearing let him say: Come. And the [one] thirsting let him come, the [one] wishing let him take water of life freely.
pieces: The Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" And whoever hears should say, "Come!" Whoever is thirsty should come; whoever wants it should take the water of life, free of charge.

L.17: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" And let the one who hears say, "Come!" And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who wishes take the water of life freely.

R.17: The Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" Everyone who hears this should say, "Come!" Anyone who is thirsty may come. Anyone who wants the water of life may take it as a free gift.

decisions.choice: Come! A prayer to Christ, and then an invitation
alternatives: all three are invitations to the hearers
decisions.reason: The Spirit and the bride, the church, call to Christ to come, answering his "I am coming" (22:12, 20), and every hearer is to join the prayer. Then the call turns outward: whoever is thirsty is invited to come and drink. Some read the first two calls also as invitations to the hearers.

decisions.choice: the water of life freely: Isaiah 55:1
decisions.reason: See 21:6. The book that warns so sternly ends with an open invitation.

records.source: Μαρτυρῶ ἐγὼ παντὶ τῷ ἀκούοντι τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· ἐάν τις ἐπιθῇ ἐπ’ αὐτά, ἐπιθήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς πληγὰς τὰς γεγραμμένας ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ·
records.gloss: I testify I to everyone hearing the words of the prophecy of the scroll this: if anyone adds to them, will add the God upon him the plagues the having been written in the scroll this;
pieces: To everyone who hears the words of the prophecy in this scroll I bear witness: if anyone adds to them, God will add to {{gender:them|him}} the plagues written in this scroll.

L.18: I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this scroll: if anyone adds to them, God will add to {{gender:that person|him}} the plagues written in this scroll,

R.18: I solemnly warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy in this scroll: If anyone adds anything to these words, God will give {{gender:that person|him}} the plagues written about in this scroll.

decisions.choice: do not add or take away: Deuteronomy 4:2
decisions.reason: Moses warned Israel not to add to God's commands or take away from them (Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32). The warning protects this prophecy from being changed or distorted by those who copy and teach it.
"I" may be Jesus, who "testifies to these things" (22:20), or John, the book's witness (22:8). Either way the warning carries Christ's authority.
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.

records.source: καὶ ἐάν τις ἀφέλῃ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τοῦ βιβλίου τῆς προφητείας ταύτης, ἀφελεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως τῆς ἁγίας, τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ.
records.gloss: and if anyone takes away from the words of the scroll of the prophecy this, will take away the God the part of him from the tree of the life and out of the city the holy, of the things having been written in the scroll this.
pieces: And anyone who removes words from the scroll of this prophecy, God will remove {{gender:their|his}} part in the tree of life and in the holy city that this scroll describes.

L.19: and if anyone takes away from the words of the scroll of this prophecy, God will take away {{gender:their|his}} share from the tree of life and from the holy city, which are written in this scroll.

R.19: If anyone takes away any words from this scroll of prophecy, God will take away that person's share in the tree of life and in the holy city that are written about in this scroll.

decisions.reason: The SBLGNT and the Greek manuscripts read "the tree of life". "The book of life", found in some printed editions and in the King James Version, has almost no support in Greek manuscripts. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
As in 1:11, the book is a scroll at every level.

records.source: Λέγει ὁ μαρτυρῶν ταῦτα· Ναί· ἔρχομαι ταχύ.
records.gloss: Says the [one] testifying these things: Yes, I am coming quickly.
pieces: The one who testifies to all this says, "Yes, I am coming soon!"

L.20: The one who testifies to these things says, "Yes, I am coming soon."

R.20: Jesus, who has told us these things, says, "Yes, I am coming soon!"

decisions.reason: Jesus is "the faithful witness" (1:5; 3:14), and these are his words, "I am coming soon" (22:7, 12).
Readable names him (m1).

records.source: Ἀμήν· ἔρχου, κύριε Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Amen, come, Lord Jesus.
pieces: Amen! Come, Lord Jesus!

decisions.choice: Come, Lord Jesus: the prayer of the early church
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the Aramaic prayer "Marana tha", "Our Lord, come!" (1 Corinthians 16:22), and it was used in early Christian worship. John answers Christ's promise with the church's prayer.

records.source: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων.
records.gloss: The grace of the Lord Jesus with all.
pieces: May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with everyone.

L.21: The grace of the Lord Jesus [be] with all.

R.21: May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with all of you.

decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "with all". Other manuscripts read "with all the saints" or "with you all", and many add "Amen". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
The book ends as letters to the churches ended (compare 1:4; Romans 16:20). Its last word is grace.
